scenario.opening_question: What matters most to us when picking a language course for the exchange semester?

options.name: Intensive Spanish Course at Madrid Language Institute
options.upside: Fast progress due to high weekly hours and immersion in Spain
options.tradeoff: Higher intensity may be exhausting alongside exchange studies
options.concern: Smaller class size might limit diversity of speaking partners

options.name: Conversational French Workshop at Lyon Community Center
options.upside: Affordable and focused on practical speaking skills
options.tradeoff: Lower weekly hours may slow overall language progress
options.concern: Larger class size could reduce individual attention

options.name: German Academic Language Prep at Berlin University
options.upside: Strong focus on academic language skills for university success
options.tradeoff: Less emphasis on casual conversation and cultural immersion
options.concern: High cost at the budget limit might restrict other activities

options.name: Japanese Language and Culture Course at Kyoto Language School
options.upside: Balanced language learning with cultural experiences included
options.tradeoff: Moderate weekly hours might not satisfy those wanting rapid fluency
options.concern: Cultural activities could reduce time for focused language study
options.best_for: learners valuing cultural context alongside language

shared_context: The exchange semester starts in September and lasts 4 months
Each participant has a budget limit of 1200 USD for the language course
The decision group consists of exactly 3 participants aiming to improve language skills for daily life and academic use
